what_its_for: This medicine gives your body the fats and calories it needs when you cannot eat normally or get enough nutrition by mouth. It is used as part of a nutrition plan given directly into your vein (called TPN or parenteral nutrition). It helps your body get energy, supports brain function, and prevents a deficiency of essential fatty acids your body cannot make on its own.
how_to_take: This medicine is given only by a healthcare professional or trained nurse through a tube placed in your vein (IV line). You will NOT give this to yourself at home unless a healthcare team has specially trained you for home IV therapy. The medicine is dripped slowly into your vein over several hours. Never shake or mix the bag yourself. Always check the bag for any particles, color changes, or separation of the liquid before it is used — if it looks unusual, tell your nurse right away.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose based on your weight, age, medical condition, and how many calories you need each day. Adults typically receive up to 2.5 grams of fat per kilogram of body weight per day. Children and newborns receive lower doses carefully calculated by their doctor. The infusion is usually given over 12 to 24 hours per day. Never adjust the drip rate on your own — always ask your nurse if something seems wrong.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given in a hospital or clinic setting by healthcare professionals, missed doses are managed by your care team. If you are on home IV therapy and you miss a scheduled infusion, call your home health nurse or doctor right away. Do not try to 'catch up' by running the infusion faster than prescribed, as this can be dangerous.
storage: The bags are stored in a cool, dry place away from light, usually between 36°F and 77°F (2°C to 25°C). Do not freeze the bags. Your pharmacy or nurse will handle storage and preparation. Once the bag is opened or connected to your IV line, it should be used within 24 hours. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not eat or drink large amounts of fatty foods right before or during your infusion without your doctor's approval. Avoid letting anyone other than your trained care team handle or adjust the IV equipment. Do not use alcohol while receiving this therapy without your doctor's guidance. Avoid activities that could dislodge your IV line, such as heavy lifting or rough movements near the IV site.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or nurse immediately if you notice: fever, chills, or shaking during or after the infusion; chest pain or trouble breathing; fast heartbeat; dizziness or feeling faint; redness, swelling, pain, or warmth at the IV site; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark urine or pale stools; unusual bruising or bleeding; severe headache; nausea or vomiting that won't stop; or if the IV bag looks cloudy, has particles, or the liquid appears to have separated into layers.
when_it_works: Your body begins using the nutrients from this medicine almost immediately during the infusion. You may start to feel more energy and strength over days to weeks as your overall nutrition improves. Your doctor will check your blood regularly to make sure the fat levels in your blood are within a safe range and that the treatment is working properly.
special_populations: Newborns and premature babies: Extra care is needed because their bodies process fats more slowly. Doses are very carefully calculated and monitored. Elderly patients: May need slower infusion rates and closer monitoring of blood fat levels. Patients with liver disease: Use with caution; your doctor will monitor liver function closely. Patients with diabetes: Blood sugar and fat levels need careful monitoring. Patients with egg or soy allergy: Tell your doctor before use, as some formulas contain egg or soy-derived ingredients. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients: Use only if your doctor determines it is necessary and safe for you and your baby.
